meta.scene_summary: We are busy building the future of AI while the rest of our stack is busy reliving the greatest hits of the nineties.

cooking.headline: Anthropic is preparing for an IPO, because apparently the AI arms race needs a public stock ticker to thrive.
cooking.summary: Anthropic is heading toward a public listing, moving from 'research lab with a mission' to 'company that now has to explain its quarterly earnings to people in suits.' It's the classic transition from solving AGI safety to making sure the line on the graph goes up for the investors. More details in the original article.
cooking.plain_english: The artificial intelligence company Anthropic is planning to offer its shares to the public on the stock market.

cooking.headline: Gemini 4 Hydrogen just dropped, because apparently we're naming models after the periodic table now.
cooking.summary: Google released a new model that promises to be faster and smarter, which is a great way to ensure your current project is obsolete by next Tuesday. It's the AI equivalent of a new iPhone release, but at least this one doesn't require a dongle.
cooking.plain_english: Google has announced the release of its latest artificial intelligence model, Gemini 4 Hydrogen.

cooked.headline: Jensen Huang resigns, and the leather jacket market just crashed
cooked.summary: The CEO who turned the world into a massive GPU cluster has stepped down amid personal scandal. It turns out even the person powering the AI revolution can't escape the legacy of human drama.
cooked.plain_english: Jensen Huang has resigned as the CEO of Nvidia following reports of an affair.

cooked.headline: Microsoft's status page is down, proving their transparency is purely performative
cooked.summary: Outlook is throwing errors, and the status page meant to tell us why is also taking a nap. It's like calling the fire department only to find out their office is currently on fire.
cooked.plain_english: Microsoft Outlook is experiencing an outage and the company's official status dashboard is also inaccessible.

cooked.headline: Apache HTTP Server just dropped a critical RCE like it's 1999
cooked.summary: It turns out the software powering half the internet still has critical holes large enough to drive a truck through. Nothing says 'stable production environment' like a vulnerability that lets strangers run whatever code they want on your server.
cooked.plain_english: A serious security flaw has been discovered in the Apache HTTP Server software that could allow unauthorized users to remotely execute malicious code.

cooked.headline: A 22-year-old PostgreSQL bug is finally old enough to legally drink
cooked.summary: This vulnerability has been hiding in the codebase since the days of dial-up internet, waiting for someone to finally notice it. It's comforting to know that our most reliable databases are essentially just ancient, haunted architecture held together by hope.
cooked.plain_english: A security vulnerability that has existed in the PostgreSQL database software for 22 years has been identified and can be exploited to run unauthorized commands.

cooked.headline: GitHub went down, and suddenly everyone had to actually remember how their CI/CD pipeline works.
cooked.summary: GitHub experienced a widespread outage affecting Webhooks and Actions, forcing developers to confront the terrifying reality of their own build processes. It turns out that when the internet's favorite remote control stops working, we all just stare at our screens and wait for the status page to turn green.
cooked.plain_english: GitHub experienced technical issues that caused service disruptions for many of its automated tools and features.

cooked.headline: Nintendo is treating GitHub like a boss level they need to speedrun with a DMCA hammer.
cooked.summary: Nintendo just nuked a massive pile of emulator repositories from GitHub, proving they'd rather delete history than let you play it on a PC. It's like being the kid who takes the ball home because they're losing, except the ball is a 20-year-old console firmware.
cooked.plain_english: Nintendo has issued legal requests to remove software from GitHub that allows users to play Nintendo games on non-Nintendo devices.

cooked.headline: Microsoft Defender is just a very enthusiastic intern stealing your source code
cooked.summary: Microsoft's security scanner was caught uploading unreleased private software to the cloud without asking for permission. It's like having a bodyguard who decides to bring your diary to the local library just to make sure it doesn't contain any secrets.
cooked.plain_english: A developer discovered that Microsoft Defender automatically uploaded their private, unreleased software to Microsoft's servers for analysis without explicit user consent.

cooked.headline: Azure is doing its best impression of a weekend server crash
cooked.summary: Users are reporting widespread Azure outages, reminding everyone that even the biggest cloud providers aren't immune to the classic 'have you tried turning it off and on again?' dilemma. If you were looking for an excuse to step away from your terminal today, the infrastructure gods have finally granted your wish.
cooked.plain_english: Multiple users are reporting service disruptions across Microsoft's Azure cloud platform.
